name: Gas lift
principle: Compressed gas is injected into the production tubing through valves in mandrels to lighten the fluid column so the well flows. About 10% of US oil wells with insufficient reservoir pressure use gas lift, and side-pocket mandrels let valves be changed by wireline.

process_steps.name: Produce and separate; recycle the gas

performance.metric: US oil wells using gas lift

source.note: Wikipedia, Gas lift, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: gas lift depth and rate capability
performance.unit: m (up to 15,000 ft); up to 30,000 bbl/d

source.note: Wikipedia, Artificial lift, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: overall system efficiency of gas lift vs other artificial lift methods
performance.basis: IPIECA Energy Efficiency Compendium, artificial lift entry (2023), Table 1: gas lift 35% overall system efficiency; comparison: sucker rod pumps 45-60%, progressive cavity pumps 70-80%, ESPs 30-70%, hydraulic pumps 20-35%, plunger lift 75-85%. The compendium defines injected-gas scf/bbl-of-liquid as the KPI but publishes no benchmark value for it

source.note: IPIECA Energy Efficiency Compendium, Artificial lift (2023) (read 2026-10-28)

advantages: Tolerates sand and deviated wells; few moving downhole parts (general)
limitations: Needs a gas source and compressor
